item.title: 哥伦比亚西部发生7.4级地震，建筑物倒塌，造成至少79人死亡
item.description:
▶Terremoto en Colombia: Sigue la cobertura de AP en español.
BOGOTA, Colombia (AP) — A powerful 7.4 magnitudeearthquakestruck westernColombiaon Monday, killing at least 111 people and damaging hundreds of buildings, President Abelardo de la Espriella said.
The president declared an emergency, which will expedite funding for the quake recovery, and said he would visit the disaster zone, centered round the rural region of Choco.
THIS IS A BREAKING NEWS UPDATE. AP’s earlier story follows below.
BOGOTA, Colombia (AP) — A powerful 7.4 magnitudeearthquakestruck westernColombiaon Monday, killing at least 79 people, trapping residents under debris of collapsed buildings and forcing people to evacuate their homes as far as the capital of Bogotá.
The epicenter was in San Jose Del Palmar, a community of about 4,800 people in the Choco region about 250 miles (400 kilometers) west of Bogota, the U.S. Geological Survey and Colombia’s counterpart reported. The USGS said it struck at a depth of 66 miles (107 kilometers). The quake also was felt in neighboring Ecuador and Panama, though minimal damage was reported there.
Local officials confirmed that at least 40 people were killed in the Risaralda region, where the hard-hit city of Pereira is located, and 27 people in the Valle del Cauca region, where Colombia’s third-biggest city, Cali, is located. At least three of those killed in Valle del Cauca were children, the governor said.
Authorities also confirmed nine people were killed in Choco, two more in the Caldas region and a 73-year-old in the Antioquia region. Many more people across the country were injured.
The quake left cities across the west of the country — Pereira, Quibdo, Cali and Manizales — ravaged. Residents and search teams picked through the rubble of collapsed buildings amid concerns by authorities of aftershocks. Colombia’s interior minister said more than 20 municipalities across the country had been hit.
Colombia’s Pacific region around the quake’s epicenter lies along the“Ring of Fire”, the line of seismic faults encircling the Pacific Ocean where most of the world’s earthquakes occur. The Pacific, particularly the Choco region, is one of the poorest regions in the country. Nestled in the dense jungle, much of Choco is highly rural and only reachable by boat or plane, which may pose a problem for authorities in assessing the wider toll.
Residents stand outside the Cathedral of Manizales after it was damaged by an earthquake in Manizales, Colombia, Monday, Aug. 10, 2026.(AP Photo/John Jairo Bonilla)
Jorge Moncayo, a 64-year-old taxi driver in Cali, said he saw plumes of dust shoot up across the city as buildings collapsed. Residents and rescue workers were searching the rubble for survivors.
“My entire house shook. I’ve never lived through such a powerful earthquake,” he said. “We’re thanking God we’re alive.”
Colombia’s Geological Service said Monday that it had been “the highest magnitude earthquake registered in Colombia in the last decade” and that it had been followed by two 2.8 and 4.8 magnitude aftershocks. Authorities also reported that flights were suspended in the airports of Manizales, Quibdo, Armenia, Cartago, Buenaventura and Pereira.
Residents and rescue workers search through the rubble of a collapsed building after an earthquake struck Cali, Colombia, Monday, Aug. 10, 2026. (AP Photo/Santiago Saldarriaga)
The earthquakes left many in the Andean nation unnerved aftertwo back-to-back quakesdevastated neighboring Venezuela in late June, destroyed hundreds of buildings andkilled more than 5,000people. At the same time the quake brought down buildings in Colombia, desperate families in Venezuela continued to search the ruins for the bodies of their loved ones.
In Pereira, photos and videos published by local media showed pieces of the airport ceiling falling down on travelers taking shelter and screaming, and people running through rubble in a panic.
Pereira’s mayor, Mauricio Salazar, told a local radio station that at least 18 people had died and that many more were trapped under “a massive quantity of collapsed buildings.”
In nearby Manizales, a city in the coffee-producing mountains of Colombia, one of the towers of the neo-Gothic cathedral collapsed and fell on the nave. Jorge Eduardo Rojas, the mayor of Manizales, asked residents to stay outside in case of aftershocks.
Authorities in the rural state of Choco, the epicenter of the quake, reported injured people and damaged buildings in the capital, but provided few details.
In Cali, a city of 2 million people, Mayor Alejandro Eder said that residents were trapped in at least 19 buildings that had collapsed.
Small earthquakes, known as “temblores,” are common in central and western Colombia, but those above 6.0 magnitude are rare. In 1999, a 6.2 magnitude quake near the city of Armenia killed more than 1,100 people.
Colombia’s newly inauguratedPresident Abelardo de la Espriella said Monday that he had personally taken charge of the government’s response to the emergency in San José del Palmar following the earthquake.
“You are not alone. The state is present and taking action,” he said.
Response to the earthquake presents the first major challenge to de la Espriella, a Trump ally who was sworn in as president over the weekend.
Patients are evacuated from a hospital after an earthquake struck Cali, Colombia, Monday, Aug. 10, 2026. (AP Photo/Santiago Saldarriaga)
Messages of support rolled in from leaders across the Americas, including Mexico, Brazil, Ecuador, El Salvador and the United States.
“The Trump administration is closely monitoring the large earthquake that struck Colombia and stands ready to support the people of Colombia,” U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio wrote in a post on X.
A number of countries offered aid, and the U.N. deputy spokesman, Farhan Haq, said “we stand ready to help as needed.”
Janetsky reported from Mexico City. Associated Press writers Edith M. Lederer at the United Nations and Matthew Lee in Washington contributed.

item.title: 加拿大波特航空航班因儿童拒绝坐下并系好安全带而被取消
item.description:
多伦多（美联社）——上周，波特航空公司在加拿大的一架航班被取消，原因是一名幼儿拒绝坐下并系好安全带，迫使飞机返回航站楼，并延误了机场关闭的跑道。
这家总部位于多伦多的航空公司周日表示，父母和机组人员多次尝试将孩子固定在座位上，但没有成功，然后将飞机返回不列颠哥伦比亚省维多利亚国际机场的航站楼以带走父母和孩子。
波特表示，周四凌晨 12 点 30 分机场跑道关闭后，将父母和孩子及其行李移走，导致飞往多伦多的航班延误，迫使其余乘客下机。
波特向其他乘客道歉，他们在第二天重新预订了航班。

item.title: 特朗普嘲笑伊朗的战争赔偿要求和其他中东事态发展
item.description:
PresidentDonald Trumpon Monday scoffed at Iran’s demand for reparations for devastation caused to the country by the U.S. and Israeli bombardment over the past five months — a demand he said Tehran’s negotiators hadn’t raised until now.
Here’s a look at the latest developments in theIran warand the wider Middle East on Monday. Full coverage can be foundhere.
Trump’s social media post Monday came after Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmail Baghaei stressed that Iran will not reopen theStrait of Hormuzuntil the U.S. meets its conditions.
Tehran wantsthe U.S. to end its blockade of Iranian ports, lift economic sanctions and release Iran’s frozen assets. It also said the U.S. must pay compensation for war damage.
“It is up to the U.S. side to stop and make amends for its illegal and destructive actions,” Baghaei said.
Trump responded that he is now demanding “compensation from Iran, for all of the people that they have killed and gravely wounded with their roadside bombs and many conflicts.”
The U.S. government has blamed Iran-backed militants for the deaths and injuries of hundreds of Americans over several decades. They include a 1983 bombing that killed 241 U.S. military personnel at a Marine compound in Beirut and the deaths of at least 603 U.S. troops in Iraq between 2003 and 2011.
Trump said he also wants Tehran to compensate the families of Iranian protesters who were killed.
“I have instructed my representatives to put this firmly into any, and all, future negotiations,” Trump said in his post.
The closure of the Strait of Hormuz — through which roughly one-fifth of the world’s traded oil supplies passed before the war — has kept energy prices as a major focus of U.S. politics ahead of November’s midterm elections.
Iran’s president said Monday the country’s supreme leader is calling for “unity and cohesion” as the Islamic Republic faces economic hardships and sanctions stemming from itswarwith the United States.
President Masoud Pezeshkian described a nearly seven-hour meeting withAyatollah Mojtaba Khameneiin an interview with Iranian state television that aired amid apparenttensions among the Islamic Republic’s leaders.
Pezeshkian told the state-run IRIB that he and Khamenei discussed “people’s livelihoods, the state of the market, employment, people’s housing,” as well as “problems that are now being created as a result of the (U.S.) sanctions.” He didn’t say when or where they met.
Most important, he said, was Khamenei’s emphasis on unity.
“All of the enemy’s plans are aimed at creating division,” Pezeshkian said. “What we have to do is prevent divisions from emerging.”
It is only the second time the Iranian president said he has met with the new supreme leader since Khamenei was appointed in March following a U.S.-Israeli strike that killed his father. Khamenei, believed to have been wounded in the same attack, has not appeared in public since then.
Iran on Sunday appointed Mohsen Rezaei, a military adviser to its new supreme leader, to head its powerful Supreme National Security Council.
Rezaei commanded Iran’s paramilitary Revolutionary Guard from 1981 to 1997, a period that includes Iran’s 1980s war with Iraq. The 71-year-old hardliner last week threatened American forces with “serious risks and casualties” if the U.S. did not lift its blockade of Iranian ports.
Rezaei replaces Mohammad Bagher Zolghadr, who will become a political adviser to Khamenei.
While Rezaei appears willing to negotiate with the U.S. to “secure Iran’s maximalist aims, including control of the Strait of Hormuz,” he has also been “unwilling to present any Iranian concessions,” wrote the Institute for the Study of War, a U.S.-based think-tank.
Israel’s military said Monday it had declared aChristian-majority townin the occupied West Bank a closed military zone to keep out Israeli settlers and other non-residents.
The new tactic is designed to keep Israelis out of Taybeh, which has been subject to arson, vandalism and settlers coming onto private and village property. The army said Palestinian residents and journalists would be allowed unless soldiers determine their presence poses a threat. The army said its troops would detain suspects and disperse gatherings to keep the peace.
The designation comes after months of the army and police struggling to maintain order throughout the territory, where at least 87 Palestinians have been killed by Israeli settlers or soldiers in 2026, according to the Ramallah-based Palestinian Health Ministry.
Yemen’s Iran-backedHouthi rebelsattacked a Red Sea port town controlled by government forces on Sunday, killing seven and injuring 30 people. Yemen’s Defense Ministry — which operates under its internationally recognized government — said four military personnel and three civilians were killed.
Clashes continued Monday near the village of Taiz. The Houthi group said a 13-year-old child was killed by artillery shelling and another child was injured.
The attack on Mokha is the latest inone of the largest wavesof Houthi strikes on Yemeni military positions and areas held by the Saudi-backed government since a 2022 truce. It comes as threats to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz have renewed focus on the Red Sea and Bab el-Mandeb Strait at its southern tip.

item.title: 扎克伯格发言人表示，他的游艇没有听到海事援助的呼叫
item.description:
马克·扎克伯格拥有的一艘游艇没有立即回应阿拉斯加海岸附近一艘燃油耗尽的小船的求救信号，但一位海事法专家周一表示，在海岸警卫队确定该船并未遇险后，他们可能没有义务做出回应。
Meta首席执行官的一位发言人还表示，船员们没有立即听到无线电求救，当听到时，附近的另一艘船已经提供了援助。
美国海岸警卫队表示，这艘 21 英尺长的 Hewescraft 船通过所有船只都应监听的无线电频率求救，并未遇险，在 Wilderness Legacy 游轮将其拖到法拉格特湾并帮助其加油后，它能够安全抵达法拉格特湾。但这起事件之所以引起关注，是因为游轮上的一名乘客在社交媒体上发帖暗示扎克伯格的游艇拒绝提供帮助。
当另一艘船遇险时，该地区的每个人都有义务做出反应，只要这样做不会使自己的船面临风险。但海事法专家伊恩·拉尔比表示，这种情况似乎有所不同，扎克伯格游艇的船员不会面临这项法律义务。
“这就是拨打 AAA 和拨打 911 的区别。你需要现场救护车，这是求救电话。你需要有人来救你或者拖你的车，你就拨打 AAA，”Auxilium Worldwide 总裁 Ralby 说。他说，就紧急情况类型而言，这是一个很大的区别。“两者都令人担忧，都需要援助，但回应的法律义务却截然不同。”
8 月 3 日晚，此事发生时，扎克伯格和他的家人并不在 387 英尺长的 Launchpad 游艇上。
扎克伯格的发言人布莱恩·贝克 (Brian Baker) 表示：“正如海岸警卫队指出的那样，这艘船并没有遇险，当船员们通过与他们操作的无线电频道不同的无线电频道查看海岸警卫队的联系信息时，援助已经开始了。我们很感激各方都安全。”
《阿拉斯加灯塔》首先报道了迈克尔·洛夫 (Michael Love) 8 月 5 日在 Bluesky 上发布的事件，迈克尔·洛夫自称是荒野遗产号游轮上的乘客。
“我们的船昨晚营救了一艘搁浅的船只，显然是在海岸警卫队通过无线电向马克·扎克伯格的游艇发出无线电信号（距离更近）后我们才采取行动，但他们一再拒绝回应。（当船长宣布这一消息时，几乎全场响起了一致的嘘声），”他说。
海岸警卫队在一份声明中表示，在小船通过无线电发出无线电信号后半小时内，他们确定这艘小船并未遇险。代表他们广播了海上援助请求，荒野遗产号做出了回应，大约一小时后到达了这艘 21 英尺长的船只。
Launchpad 船员错过求救信号有点不寻常，因为船舶通常会始终监听无线电上的 16 频道并将其保留为默认频率。这是发出求救信号的地方，也是海岸警卫队发布有关该地区任何危险的警告的地方，无论是正在酝酿的风暴还是其他任何危险。
拉尔比说：“情况得到了解决，没有对生命造成任何伤害。”“在对海员生命的威胁或对海洋环境的担忧方面，似乎没有任何直接问题，这是导致紧急求救呼叫的两个主要因素，所有海员，无论是谁，都有法律义务尝试做出回应。”

item.title: 野火席卷美国西部和加拿大，居民被疏散
item.description:
周日，美国西部和加拿大燃烧的野火使一些居民警惕可能的疏散命令，而其他已经被迫逃离家园的人则等待着看看他们回来后会剩下什么。
在加拿大西部，周末，由于快速蔓延的野火摧毁了房屋，超过 20,000 人被迫逃离不列颠哥伦比亚省奥肯那根湖沿岸的社区，数十人不得不通过飞机救援。在美国，华盛顿的工作人员已经在斯波坎地区扑灭了三场野火，这三场野火在斯波坎地区燃烧了一个多星期，他们继续在遏制线附近进行清理工作。
上周末，劳里·艾伦 (Laurie Allen) 离开位于斯波坎北部社区九英里瀑布 (Nine Mile Falls) 的家，带着丈夫、狗和两只小猫逃离了不远处发生的野火。周日，通往她所在社区的道路仍然关闭，但她说她从一位朋友那里得知，虽然她的房子和附近的其他房子都被灰烬覆盖，但都完好无损。
“我在这里已经 65 年了。这从来没有发生过，”艾伦说。“我们没有考虑任何事情，只是抓住我们的动物然后离开。但现在它影响了我们周围的很多朋友和家人。所以这是相当毁灭性的。”
在加拿大，安妮特·鲍莱特 (Anette Boulet) 是逃离萨默兰 (Summerland) 的居民之一。萨默兰位于不列颠哥伦比亚省奥肯那根湖 (Okanagan Lake) 沿岸，居住着约 12,000 人。周六凌晨 4 点 30 分左右，当她和家人离开时，他们的家被烟雾笼罩。
2026 年 8 月 8 日星期六晚，秃岭野火的热点在不列颠哥伦比亚省萨默兰房屋上方的山腰上燃烧。（Darryl Dyck/加拿大媒体，美联社）
“你几乎看不见。当时天很黑，山脊，火山脊正向你袭来，”疏散到彭蒂克顿中心的鲍莱特说。
“没有言语可以表达它，”她说。“恐惧。”
周日晚些时候，加拿大皇家骑警表示，一名 80 岁的妇女在试图逃离奥肯那根湖地区被迫疏散的野火时死亡。
除了萨默兰 (Summerland) 的疏散工作外，周五晚上首次报道的巴尔德山脉 (Bald Range) 火灾也导致皮奇兰 (Peachland) 及其周边地区约 ​​8,000 人疏散。不列颠哥伦比亚省周六宣布进入紧急状态。
加拿大应急管理和社区复原力部长埃莉诺·奥尔谢夫斯基周日在社交媒体上表示，她已批准不列颠哥伦比亚省的联邦援助请求，为被迫逃离的人提供庇护所和住宿。
2026 年 8 月 8 日星期六，在不列颠哥伦比亚省彭蒂克顿，格雷格·克劳特 (Greg Krauter) 因巴尔德山脉 (Bald Range) 野火而被迫在半夜带着七只山羊撤离萨默兰 (Summerland) 的房产，他在卡车后座检查其中的一些山羊，而其他山羊则在不列颠哥伦比亚省彭蒂克顿的一个疏散中心外走动。（Darryl Dyck/加拿大媒体，美联社）
据野火管理团队发布的新闻稿称，周日，扑灭斯波坎地区三场野火的工作人员继续在遏制线附近进行“扫荡行动”，没有任何火势蔓延。上周发生的大火已损坏或摧毁了约 920 座建筑物。
本周早些时候，一名男子被捕并被指控故意纵火，这是斯波坎地区三起火灾中规模最大的一场。
周六，位于斯波坎以南约 35 英里（55 公里）的乡村小镇马尔登的居民被敦促立即撤离。然而，到了周日，他们的疏散级别已降级，准备在必要时迅速撤离。
约翰·戈伊克（John Goyke）的公司根据合同经营马尔登的水，他说：“风势相当平静。火势没有蔓延，但我们正在使用社交媒体和 Facebook 与每个人保持联系。”
附近罗萨莉亚市的市长戈伊克表示，马尔登的居民被告知要节约用水，以便在需要时为消防车节省用水，马尔登消防部门一直在从罗萨莉亚运水。
2020 年，马尔登的大部分地区被野火摧毁，失去了消防站、邮局、市政厅和图书馆。
在犹他州，周五早上，两名直升机飞行员在鱼湖国家森林扑灭野火时坠毁。周六，工作人员终于能够到达现场确认死亡情况。
官员们周日表示，由于地形陡峭、崎岖，火灾导致他们无法迅速到达该地区。
塞维尔县警长内森·柯蒂斯说：“当我们第一次到达那里时，我们可以看到两股不同的烟雾，一股来自坠机现场，一股来自向我们扑来的大火。”
美国国家运输安全委员会正在调查事故原因。
美联社记者霍莉·拉默对此报道做出了贡献。

item.title: 国会民主党人对驱逐美军成员及其家人的行为展开调查
item.description:
国会民主党人表示，在美联社发现超过 50 名现役军人的配偶和父母被移民当局拘留后，他们正在调查特朗普政府驱逐军人及其家人的行为。
民主党在周日晚间致国土安全部、国防部和退伍军人事务部的一封信中表示，他们将调查五角大楼和国土安全部是否正在协调驱逐军人及其家人。
这封由 60 多名议员签署并提供给美联社的信称，“这些行为危及军事准备，削弱军人的士气，违背了美国对那些为国家冒生命危险的人们的承诺。”
五角大楼拒绝发表评论，表示将“直接回复这封信的作者”。
国土安全部告诉美联社，它重视军人的贡献，“美国兵役本身并不能自动授予合法移民身份，也不能免除外国人违反美国移民法的后果。”
退伍军人管理局没有立即回应置评请求。
民主党在信中向各机构提出了广泛的问题清单。他们表示，国土安全部和军方明显合作驱逐军人家属，“引起了道德和法律方面的担忧”。
马萨诸塞州参议员说：“唐纳德·特朗普撕毁了数十个承诺提供移民保护的军人家庭，破坏了我们国家对军人的承诺。”伊丽莎白·沃伦说道。“这简直太残酷了，它正在损害我们的军事准备和士气。”
沃伦的办公室正在与康涅狄格州参议员一起领导这项调查。理查德·布卢门撒尔 (Richard Blumenthal)，伊利诺伊州参议员。塔米·达克沃斯和几位众议院民主党人。
美联社的调查发现，唐纳德·特朗普总统的政府取消了对军人家属的保护，并背离了两党长期以来达成的大规模驱逐议程的共识。在配偶被拘留后，服役人员被迫休假，包括推迟部署，以照顾孩子。
议员们向政府施压，询问征兵人员为何仍在促进移民保护。
议员们援引美联社的报道，敦促特朗普政府恢复此前保护军人家属免受移民执法影响的政策，同时允许他们调整自己的法律地位。
参议院退伍军人事务委员会资深民主党人布卢门撒尔表示：“这份报告令人震惊，显示了特朗普移民议程核心令人难以置信的残酷行为。”“我们将要求答案和问责。”
武装部队和退伍军人事务委员会的共和党主席、密西西比州参议员。罗杰·威克和堪萨斯州参议员杰里·莫兰没有回应置评请求。
上周，特朗普成立了军事配偶委员会，由国防部长皮特·赫格斯的妻子詹妮弗·劳切特担任主席，负责制定改善军人配偶生活的政策和建议。
特朗普在 8 月 6 日发表在《联邦公报》上的一封信中表示，“军人配偶与我们军队的良好秩序、战备和保留有着内在的联系。他们对我们武装部队的支持和贡献对于任务的成功至关重要。”
白宫没有回应置评请求。
美联社获得的国防部在去年 12 月致民主党议员的一封信中表示，国防部最近没有对军队中的非公民家庭成员实施任何政策变化，也没有对驱逐出境如何影响部队战备和士气进行分析。
为面临驱逐的军人家属和退伍军人提供支持的组织“遣返我们的爱国者”主席达尼察·詹姆斯表示，军队正在遭到背叛。
詹姆斯说：“我们的军人是那些在虚线上签名去保卫我们的国家，但可能不会回来的人。”“他们相信我们的政府会照顾他们的家人，但他们并没有这样做。”
布鲁克是美联社/美国报道州议会新闻计划的成员。美国报道是一项非营利性国家服务计划，让记者在当地新闻编辑室报道未被揭露的问题。

item.title: 特朗普宣布幕僚秘书威尔·沙夫将担任他的新任白宫法律顾问
item.description:
华盛顿（美联社）——唐纳德·特朗普总统周日宣布，他的新任白宫法律顾问将是幕僚秘书威尔·沙夫（Will Scharf），他作为特朗普任命的国家资本规划委员会主席，帮助确保了这项价值 4 亿美元的宴会厅项目的批准。
特朗普表示，从 9 月 1 日开始，沙夫将接替大卫·沃灵顿，后者将离开政府加入私营部门。特朗普指出，沙夫此前曾担任联邦检察官，并在包括最高法院在内的许多案件中代表他。
“意志是坚韧、坚强和聪明的！他也热爱我们的国家，并尊重法律，”特朗普在《真相社会》上写道。“威尔·沙夫作为白宫法律顾问会做得很好！”
白宫法律顾问办公室的改组正值关键时刻——距离中期选举仅几个月，特朗普领导的共和党将奋力保住国会的控制权。民主党人誓言，如果 11 月份调查成功，将对特朗普及其政府展开调查。
白宫法律顾问的工作是就与总统职位相关的法律和政策问题提供建议。该办公室是司法部在白宫的主要联系人，负责处理总统赦免、司法任命和审查立法。该办公室还帮助调查和管理国会对政府的调查以及总统以官方身份被起诉时针对总统的诉讼。
在特朗普的第一个任期内，沙夫努力让法官和大法官得到确认。其中包括美国最高法院法官布雷特·卡瓦诺（Brett Kavanaugh）（他本人曾担任乔治·W·布什总统的白宫幕僚秘书）和艾米·科尼·巴雷特（Amy Coney Barrett）。
在特朗普卸任期间，沙夫于2023年10月加入他的法律团队，并在特别检察官杰克·史密斯提起的选举干扰案中担任他的律师之一。此案提交最高法院，最高法院裁定总统享有全面的豁免权，免受因官方行为而受到刑事起诉。
沙夫是特朗普第二届政府中获得职位的几位律师之一。托德·布兰奇（Todd Blanche）在纽约共和党封口费审判中代表特朗普，上周被确认担任司法部长。
作为白宫幕僚秘书，沙夫负责管理总统办公桌上的文件。当总统签署行政命令时，他站在特朗普身边，并经常对特朗普签署的内容进行连续旁白。
特朗普于 2025 年 7 月任命沙夫为国家首都规划委员会主席，该委员会是负责该地区政府建筑建设和重大翻修的行政部门机构。
特朗普的舞厅于 4 月份获得了 NCPC 的最终批准，尽管联邦上诉法院周五裁定，该项目的建设必须停止，因为国会尚未批准该项目。特朗普发誓要向美国最高法院提起上诉。
该项目已经进展顺利，并开始在白宫东侧拔地而起。

item.title: 华盛顿努力将国民警卫队部署延长至 2029 年
item.description:
WASHINGTON (AP) — It’s been 12 months since President Donald Trump announceda crime emergencyin Washington, pledging to make the city “safe and beautiful” and deploying the National Guard.
But a mission that seemed temporary has beenextended through January 2029. Residents anda new cadre of local officialssee in it an unacceptable attempt by the federal government to restrict the heavily Democratic city’s autonomy and, a year in, still question why having troops on the streets of the nation’s capital is necessary.
“There’s a deep irony that here we are in the capital of the free world, and our president is treating it like a police state,” said Scott Michelman, legal director of the ACLU of the District of Columbia. “D.C. residents have lived with our National Guard troops in our neighborhoods for about a year, despite the absence of any genuine emergency and really any reason for them to be here.”
The continued deployment will be a major test for a new batch of political candidates expected to take office after the midterms this fall. Residents will look to them to push back on the Republican president’s encroachment into the city’s affairs — although they’re limited in what they can do to counter it.
On Aug. 11, 2025, Trump announced he was launchinga federal law enforcement surgein Washington aimed at fighting crime. As of Aug. 4, more than 4,600 military personnel from D.C. and 24 states and territories were still deployed alongside unknown numbers of less visible federal law enforcement officers. Some are expected to be withdrawn toward the end of the summer.
Small groups of armed guard members have become a routine presence on the streets. They have supported arrest operations but are also seen patrolling tourist areas, such as along the Tidal Basin duringthe Cherry Blossom Festivaland in neighborhoods such as Georgetown where violent crimes are rare. They’ve helped with medical emergencies, snow removal and beautification projects — initiatives that havereceived supportfrom some residents.
Extending the deployment into 2029 will cost about $1.4 billion, the Defense Department estimates. Exact figures on what’s been spent so far are unavailable, but the Congressional Budget Office projected in a report earlier this year the total cost for the first year of the deployment would be around $660 million, based on a monthly troop level of about 2,900, a figure that’s fluctuated throughout the mission.
“President Trump has transformed D.C. from a crime-ridden city into a safe and beautiful haven for residents and visitors alike,” White House spokeswoman Abigail Jackson said in an email.
Figures posted to the U.S. attorney’s office for the District of Columbia credit the surge with more than 13,000 arrests.
Crime, which was falling before the surge began, continues to drop. Metropolitan Police Department statistics show overall crime was down 20% through Friday, compared with the same period in 2025. That includes a 32% drop in homicides, from 97 to 66.
But there’s a debate over how much of that success is owed to Trump’s mission or to yearslong local efforts to chip away at the crime rate.
What’s certain is locals feel the weight of the deployment and don’t see a clear way to push back against it. National Guard deployments to other cities have been blocked by courts, anda lawsuit challenging the deploymentis pending, but critics of the surge aren’t hopeful.
“The fact that we still have the National Guard walking our streets a year later with no end in sight is really demoralizing,” city council member Brianne K. Nadeau said.
Because Washington is a congressionally established federal district, Trump has much greater influence over the police and D.C. National Guard, which he controls directly, including its commander.
The Home Rule Act, passed in 1973, allows residents to vote for local leaders, including the mayor and council members. Congress has oversight over the local budget and review authority of all laws passed and the ability to summon district officials to the Capitol routinely to explain themselves.The D.C. delegate to Congressis a nonvoting position.
The city’s governmental structure under home rule made it easy for Trump to do what he has done, Nadeau said.
“There isn’t really any political liability for national leaders to mess with D.C. because nobody really cares,” outside of those directly impacted, she said.
The law enforcement surge played a major role inDemocratic primary electionsin June, which elevated candidates who have made Washington’s autonomy and statehood top priorities.
Janeese Lewis George, a democratic socialist who in the overwhelmingly Democratic city is likely to be its next mayor, has already rankled Trump. He threatened to put the city under federal control if she wins.
Robert White Jr., another pro-statehood candidate, won the Democratic primary for the city’s seat in Congress.
And while they are hamstrung by the city’s status, both hope they have strategies that can help fight back against the president and the deployment.
White told The Associated Press he plans to build “an army of residents” and allies to target swing districts and work at “un-electing” people critical of the district and “electing those who do support D.C.”
The action is similar to one a former D.C. congressional delegate, Walter Fauntroy, successfully pursued in 1972, mobilizing Black voters and allies against a South Carolina Congress member who had long opposed D.C.'s independence.
“He didn’t deploy that strategy a bunch of times, but it sent a signal to people to lay off of D.C.,” White said.
The city’s outgoing mayor,Muriel Bowser, avoided the kind of biting rhetoric and personal attacks typical of other high-profile Democratic leaders, despite the unprecedented intervention into her city. A major part of that was to avoid raising Trump’s ire and threaten what independence the city has.
An emailed statement from Bowser’s office said that despite challenges to its independence the city has progressed in achieving its goals. “The safety and well-being of everyone in our city remains our top priority and protecting home rule remains our North Star,” the statement said.
“We’re more than monuments and politics,” Bowser said in a 48-second video pinned to her X account.
She said the city is made up of more than 700,00 taxpaying Americans who serve in the military, run businesses and raise families and “we don’t have voting representation in Congress. We don’t control the D.C. National Guard, and we don’t have full access to full American democracy.”
Donna Powell, who is living part time in the city, said she and her husband walk and metro everywhere. “We’re already safe and beautiful,” she said. “We don’t need all these National Guard here.”
The money could be better spent “on healthcare and food for families that need it.”
The National Guard deployment has raised concerns among some over what the upcoming midterms and the 2028 presidential election will look like with troops on the streets.
“The last time this president was supposed to come out of power, Jan. 6 happened,” said Alex Dodds, co-founder of FreeDC, an activist group that has protested the deployment by following and filming National Guard troops in quiet areas of the city far away from crime concerns. “Imagine if that happens again but this time he has 5,000 troops standing at the ready to be part of that situation. You know, that’s our worry.”

item.title: 明尼苏达州参议院初选惨烈，特朗普的移民镇压迫在眉睫
item.description:
MINNEAPOLIS (AP) — In the streets surrounding a drab federal office complex next to the Minneapolis airport, the beleaguered resistance toPresident Donald Trumpfound its footing.
As U.S. immigration agents staged at the Bishop Henry Whipple Federal Building for a monthslongdeportation campaign, protesters with whistles and cellphone cameras assembled to oppose them.Two were shot and killedin the city’s streets before Trump pulled back under pressure.
Months later, those confrontations remain the backdrop to Minnesota’sDemocratic primary for U.S. Senateon Tuesday, which features establishment-backed U.S. Rep. Angie Craig and the more progressive Lt. Gov. Peggy Flanagan. The immigration debate is an added schism in a race that otherwise echoes many of the other left versus center divides that have played out across the United States this year.
Protesters stand on the side of the road with ICE protest signs, Jan. 19, 2026, in St. Paul, Minn. (AP Photo/Angelina Katsanis, File)
Craig voted for tighter enforcement soon after Trump returned to office last year, only to later express regret for her decision after the Republican president sent a surge of agents into Minneapolis. She backed a resolution that condemned antisemitism after a2025 firebombingin Boulder, Colorado, and expressed thanks for law enforcement, including U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement officers.
Those votes may turn out to be some of the most fraught of Craig’s eight-year career in Congress, decisions that Flanagan has highlighted while trying to portray her rival as unwilling to fight an unpopular administration in Washington.
“I think that’s when she lost my vote permanently and that’s why I will not vote for her no matter what,” said Bryce Bohne, 40, of Minneapolis. The teacher and owner of an educational tourism company is supporting Flanagan.
Around the Whipple federal building, the fences and barriers are down. The ambient soundtrack is no longer the whistles and chants of protesters, just the rumble of departing jets and passing buses.
But the signs of what happened remain. A few volunteers in bright orange vests keep vigil across the street for 12-plus hours a day, ready to help people getting released from immigration detention or leaving hearings at the immigration court inside.
A few miles away, visitors still bring fresh flowers and handwritten notes to memorials marking the spotswhere Renee GoodandAlex Prettiwere killed.
A demonstrator holds a sign reading “Justice for Renee & Alex” during a protest outside a SpringHill Suites and Residence Inn by Marriott hotels, Jan. 26, 2026, in Maple Grove, Minn. (AP Photo/Adam Gray, File)
Craig flipped a Republican-held seat in 2018, and every two years she overcame millions of dollars of attack ads to win tough reelection campaigns.
Until Craig’s Senate run, the heat came from the right. Newly under fire from the other side, the decisions she made as a swing-seat congresswoman have become a liability as a statewide Senate candidate. At one recent event, she adopted the language of the insurgent left, though it did not always seem to come naturally.
“The working class keeps getting screwed,” she told volunteers preparing to knock on doors for her Saturday in Brooklyn Park, a Minneapolis suburb. “Folks, I don’t know about you, but it is time that we had a working folks reno— reso— renovation—"
U.S. Rep. Angie Craig, D-Minn., a candidate for U.S Senate, speaks to constituents during a door-knocking event Saturday, July 25, 2026, in Minneapolis. (AP Photo/Ellen Schmidt)
In Craig’s view, she is well suited to the antiestablishment fervor gaining a foothold in the Democratic Party. Raised by a single mother in an Arkansas trailer park, she has known economic hardship. The lesbian mother of four grown children, she is not the archetype of a traditional member of Congress.
She was one of the House Democrats to call for President Joe Biden to drop out of the 2024 race after his disastrous debate performance against Trump. As a relatively junior member of Congress, she pushed successfully to become the top Democrat on the Agriculture Committee, jumping ahead of long-tenured colleagues.
“I consider myself a progressive” she told reporters after her event Saturday. “Every race that I run, Republicans run ads against me saying I vote with Democrats 96, 97% of the time.”
“Of course, in the primary,” she added, “people want to point out the few votes I’ve taken against Democrats.”
Chief among them was theLaken Riley Act, the first bill passed by Congress after Trump started his second term. It requires federal authorities to detain migrants accused of theft and violent crimes.
Craig and nearly 60 other Democrats in the House and Senate voted for the bill early in 2025.
But at the end of the year, as immigration officers descended on Minneapolis, that vote became a liability. Weeks after Good and Pretti were killed, Craig published a mea culpa in a Minnesota Star Tribune column.
Craig explained that although she had qualms with parts of the law, it had the support of Democrats she respected, and many of her constituents were unhappy with the situation on the border under Biden.
But the “outright occupation by aggressive, unaccountable federal forces” made clear to her “that supporting any bill that gives ICE new authority in this administration was the wrong decision. And I regret my vote.”
Trump’s immigration operation, she says, was not enabled by her vote on the Laken Riley Act.
“Before that, people had a little bit more sensibility about the fact she was in a tough district and had to take tough votes,” said Corey Day, former executive director of the Minnesota Democratic-Farmer-Labor Party.
Craig has since presented herself as a strong defender of Minnesotans against Trump. She says her record of winning tough races positions her to ensure the seat stays in Democratic hands.
“Angie has experience working across demographics that we need to win over statewide, including in rural Minnesota,” said Kevin Anderson, a Hennepin County commissioner who is supporting Craig and went to one of her weekend events. “I love Peggy, I really do, she’s a great politician. But I don’t think she’s ever had to work across Minnesota.”
Democratic Gov. Tim Walz has declined to endorse either candidate for the seat held by Democrat Tina Smith, who is not running again. Late last month his wife, Gwen Walz, endorsed Craig over Flanagan, his governing partner for two terms.
The Republican field includesMichele Tafoya, a former NFL sideline reporter.
Minnesota Lt. Gov. Peggy Flanagan, a Democratic candidate for U.S. Senate, listens to a voter during a campaign event at the Leech Lake Band of Ojibwe Twin Cities Office in Minneapolis, Saturday, Aug. 8, 2026. (AP Photo/Ellen Schmidt)
To Flanagan and her supporters, Craig’s vote for the immigration bill was not a pragmatic overture to swing voters but a betrayal.
“My primary opponent voted for Donald Trump’s immigration bill and was the only Minnesota Democrat to do so,” Flanagan told volunteers in St. Paul on Saturday. “She since then has said that she regrets that vote, and I’m glad. But it shouldn’t have taken 14 months.”
“We can stand with the immigrant community and not just when it’s politically expedient for us,” Flanagan added.
Like Abdul El-Sayed, who won last week’s Democratic Senate primary in Michigan, Flanagan supports Medicare for All and wants to curtail U.S. military support for Israel. She is running as much against the donors who have spent millions of dollars backing Craig as she is against Craig herself.
“The fact that the money is coming from us and only us makes such a huge difference, because she’s beholden to us, not some billionaire with some business or crypto interest,” said 43-year-old Flanagan supporter Justin Ropella, a customer service manager from Woodbury.
Through July 22, Craig’s campaign had spent $9 million and Flanagan’s $5.5 million. The disparity was even higher among outside groups, with Craig backers spending considerably more, though both have benefited from an influx of outside spending.
To help make up the difference, Flanagan has called on the support of progressive champions such as Sen. Bernie Sanders the Vermont independent who campaigned with her last month.
“If the people of Minnesota can stand up -- and I’m confident that they can -- and tell these billionaires and their lies and their 30-second ads and their super PACs to go to hell, democracy is going to reign,” Sanders said.

item.title: 勇士队王牌克里斯·塞尔在对阵洋基队的比赛开始前被裁判丹·默泽尔驱逐出场
item.description:
纽约（美联社）——在周日对阵纽约洋基队的比赛中，亚特兰大勇士队的王牌球员克里斯·塞尔在投球前被裁判丹·默泽尔驱逐出场，一天前，他因投球得分而被吹罚投球。
当裁判员走上球场，走过勇士队三垒一侧的休息区时，塞尔开始吠叫。默泽尔把他扔了下去，塞尔对机组长丹·贝利诺说了些什么，两人在休息室栏杆附近交谈。
“我在球棒架旁，因为比赛即将开始，我正在拿头盔，”中外野手迈克尔·哈里斯二世在他的第 10 局单打帮助亚特兰大队以 2-1 获胜后说道。“我没有看到他在和他说话，但我实际上看到了他把他扔出去的动作。我有点困惑，但后来我看到了塞尔，想起了昨天发生的事情，我把两个和两个放在一起。”
在周六5-4输掉比赛的第五局中，塞尔被梅泽尔吹罚职业生涯第三次击球。新秀斯宾塞·琼斯在打点三垒安打后击球得分，塞尔开始对默泽尔猛烈地大喊大叫，随后主教练沃尔特·韦斯继续争吵并被驱逐。
“我认为他昨天对裁判说了一些话，但你知道吗，一切都已经过去了，”韦斯说。“每个人都有自己的发言权，我们继续前进。”
贝利诺在周六的比赛结束后告诉台球记者，塞尔被要求回避，因为他没有宣布自己要在比赛结束时投球。贝利诺表示，塞尔在三振何塞·卡巴列罗时宣称自己即将投球，但在击球给奥斯汀·威尔斯之前并没有这样做。
这是塞尔职业生涯第四次被驱逐。这是他自 2019 年 8 月 3 日以来的第一次，当时他为波士顿队投球，在洋基体育场以 9-2 输掉比赛的第四局中，因争球和好球而被迈克·埃斯塔布鲁克 (Mike Estabrook) 扔下。
塞尔周六在六局比赛中失三分、五支安打，这是他自 6 月 28 日以来的第一次失利。在他为勇士队效力的第三个赛季中，这位经验丰富的左手投手在 21 场先发中取得了 12 胜 7 负的战绩，自责失分率为 2.20。

item.title: 效力凯尔特人队期间赢得 5 次总冠军的 NBA 教练唐·尼尔森去世，享年 86 岁
item.description:
Don Nelson, the second-winningest coach in NBA history who won five championships as a player with theBoston Celtics, died Sunday. He was 86.
Nelson’s family confirmed thedeathin a statement that did not say where he died or provide a cause.
“On Sunday morning our beloved husband, dad, grandfather and great-grandfather Don Nelson peacefully went to be with the Lord, surrounded by his loving family,” the statement said. “Throughout his last week, friends and family encircled him with love, sharing the blessing of his friendship and revisiting treasured memories.”
Nelson is one of two coaches in NBA history to have at least 250 wins with three different franchises —Milwaukee,DallasandGolden State— also serving as general manager for all three franchises. He was a three-time coach of the year and made the playoffs 18 times in 31 seasons. He went to the conference finals three times with the Bucks and once with the Mavericks, never winning a title.
Nelson introduced what is now known as the point forward, and his up-tempo style of offense created a buzz. He said the idea of shifting from the dominant big men of the 1970s to an offense focused on speed and the fast break came from his playing days under Celtics Hall of Fame coach Red Auerbach.
“The league really hadn’t seen an offense like the one we were running, and the results were undeniable,” Nelson wrote in 2016 in The Players’ Tribune.
Nelson said that “without Red Auerbach teaching me the mechanics of running the fast break, none of it would have been possible. He deserves all the credit for Nellie Ball, and for how fast the game of basketball is played today.”
Nelson played 11 of his 14 seasons in Boston and was on five Celtics championship teams under four different coaches. He became an assistant coach in Milwaukee after retiring as a player, then took over after coach Larry Costello resigned 18 games into the 1976-77 season. Nelson coached the Bucks for 11 seasons starting in 1976 and won seven straight division titles.
In Nelson’s second season, Milwaukee overcame a 29-point fourth quarter deficit to beat Atlanta 117-115 in regulation.
“I coached the team as though I was still playing for the Celtics, while implementing a few of my own strategies,” Nelson wrote. “I knew I wanted to play unconventional basketball and use speed to my advantage.”
His fast-paced offenses were probably best on display with Golden State in the “Run TMC” era featuring future Hall of Famers Tim Hardaway, Mitch Richmond and Chris Mullin. Nelson said he wanted them on the court at the same time.
Nelson spent 11 seasons over two stints with Golden State. The first one was punctuated by a rift with rookie star Chris Webber, who was traded away a month into his second season. Nelson, demoralized by the trade, missed nine games that season due to illness and resigned under pressure three months later in February 1995.
In between, Nelson was fired after less than one season in New York in 1995-96, then coached in Dallas for eight seasons, missing 21 games with the Mavericks starting in December 2000 to recuperate from prostate cancer surgery.
Nelson’s son, Donnie,joined his father as an assistant coach with the Mavericks in 1998, later became general manager and remained with the organization until 2021. Together they persuaded 20-year-old German starDirk Nowitzkito pass up European basketball and join the Mavericks. Don Nelson also developedSteve Nashinto one of the NBA’s top point guards before Nash went on to win back-to-back MVPs with the Phoenix Suns in 2005 and 2006.
“Don Nelson was a true innovator whose influence on the game of basketball is still felt today,” current Warriors coach Steve Kerr said. “He consistently challenged conventional thinking, experimented with different lineups and styles of play and saw possibilities in the game that others often did not. So much of what is now commonplace in the modern NBA can be traced back to the way Nellie approached the game.”
At Golden State, Nelson’s “We Believe” Warriors led by Baron Davis upset Nowitzki and the top-seeded Mavericks in the first round of the 2007 playoffs in one of the biggest shockers in NBA history. In his final season as a coach, Nelson mentored rookie Stephen Curry in 2009-10.
“One of the big reasons I was drafted by the Warriors was because of Don Nelson. The story is he never liked rookies, but from Day 1 he challenged me and gave me an opportunity to be my best self on the court,” Curry said in a statement released by the Warriors. “He taught me a lot during our one season together and I’ll never forget the night he became the winningest coach in NBA history in Minnesota. We were so happy for him. He had an immeasurable impact on the sport and will go down as one of the greatest minds in the history of the game.”
Davis added: “When I think of Nellie, I’ll always think of the ‘We Believe’ team and our incredible run in 2007. He understood what made us go and made us believe we could beat anybody, ultimately helping us make history as the first No. 8 seed to defeat a No. 1 seed in a seven-game series. That time in my life and career was truly special, and Nellie was a huge part of making it possible.”
Nelson retired as the NBA’s career coaching wins leader with 1,335, just ahead of Lenny Wilkens’ 1,332. Nelson kept that top spot for nearly 12 years before close friend and now-retired San Antonio coachGregg Popovich passed him in March 2022.
Nelson was inducted into the Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame in 2012. In 2025, hereceived the Chuck Daly Lifetime Achievement Award, presented by the National Basketball Coaches Association. Miffed that the Mavericks sent Luka Doncic to the Los Angeles Lakers in a blockbuster trade, Nelson wore a pair of Doncic’s signature Jordan Brand sneakers to the awards ceremony. He called the tradea “tremendous mistake.”
Born in Muskegon, Michigan, Nelson attended high school in Rock Island, Illinois, and averaged a double-double in college at Iowa. He spent his retirement years living on the Hawaiian island of Maui and owned several short-term rentals on the island.

item.title: 欧足联、中北美洲及加勒比地区足联和亚足联指责国际足联在世界杯计划上“欺骗”和“违反信任”
item.description:
欧足联、中北美洲及加勒比海足联和亚足联认为，国际足联主席詹尼·因凡蒂诺最近计划出售世界杯权益，这是对世界足球管理机构所服务机构的“根本性破坏”。
在周一公布的一封“致足球大家庭的公开信”中，欧足联、中北美及加勒比地区足联和亚足联还表示，“当信任因欺骗而被打破，当一个人将自己凌驾于赋予他权力的集体之上时，他的职责就被放弃了。”
欧足联在欧洲管理足球，中北美洲及加勒比海地区足球协会（CONCACAF）在北美、中美洲和加勒比地区管理足球，而亚足联则在亚洲管理足球运动。
这封信由欧足联主席亚历山大·切费林、亚足联主席萨勒曼·本·易卜拉欣·阿勒哈利法、中北美洲及加勒比海足联主席维克多·蒙塔利亚尼以及三名秘书长共同签署。
“足球是世界上最伟大的共同激情。它不属于任何个人，也不属于任何机构。它属于球员、球迷、俱乐部、会员协会和每一个受托维护其未来的机构，”公开信说。“正是本着这种精神，作为代表其成员的联合会，我们今天集体发言。”
因凡蒂诺将世界杯股份出售给私募股权投资者失败后，他面临着一场反抗。
信中说：“这不是游戏管理员的行为，而是相信游戏对他负责的人的行为。”“这些并不是足球界应有的领导品质。这就是为什么我们采取这样的立场：不是轻率、不是单独，而是团结一致，出于对我们所服务的比赛的责任。”
欧足联此前曾发出抵制世界杯和国际足联其他赛事的威胁，尽管该管理机构放弃了计划并为其失败的计划道歉。
挪威足协呼吁因凡蒂诺下台，英国足协也撤回了对因凡蒂诺明年3月连任的支持。
“足球的力量一直在于团结。我们呼吁现在就尊重这种团结，”信中说。“领导力是为足球服务，而不是寻求指挥足球。”
上周三，国际足联表示，已对失败的计划所犯的错误表示歉意，但在摩洛哥举行的危机会议上，高级工作人员“重申全力支持”他的主席任期。
不过，会议的性质也遭到批评。
公开信称：“国际足联自己的信也证实，只有一名民选官员出席了在摩洛哥举行的领导人会议。”“没有邀请国际足联理事会成员或会员协会参加。只有由国际足联聘用的高级职员组成的管理委员会出席了会议。”
国际足联还被敦促不要仅仅承认错误。
信中说：“它将此视为沟通的失败，而足球界目睹的是判断的失败。”“人们仍然没有认识到，试图出售国际足联世界杯的权益是一种严重的判断失误——不仅是程序上的失误，而且从根本上违背了国际足联所服务的机构的信任。”
在周六的一份声明中，国际足联为因凡蒂诺辩护，反对所谓的“一致和持续的努力”破坏他对组织的领导力。
此前，英国报纸《每日电讯报》曾报道过欧足联向因凡蒂诺担任欧洲足球管理机构秘书长期间与因凡蒂诺共事的一名女职员支付的离职费提出质疑。
欧足联证实已向该员工支付了“离职金”，并表示这“符合”当时的规定。
因凡蒂诺在当选国际足联主席之前在欧足联工作了 16 年。

item.title: 《蜘蛛侠：全新一天》保持创纪录节奏，《奥德赛》创诺兰新高
item.description:
纽约（美联社）——据周日电影公司估计，《蜘蛛侠：崭新的一天》继续在影院上映，第二个周末的国内​​票房就达到了 1.445 亿美元，而克里斯托弗·诺兰的《奥德赛》则创下了导演的新高。
索尼与漫威联合推出的这部影片在上映短短 10 天内就在全球收获了 16.7 亿美元的票房，有望成为有史以来最卖座的大片之一。在国内，没有哪一部电影能比这更快地获得更高的总票房。迄今为止，《全新一天》在美国和加拿大影院的票房收入已达 6.551 亿美元。在海外，这一数字已经超过10亿美元。
仅用了 7 天，《全新一天》就成为年度票房最高的电影，轻松取代《玩具总动员 5》（全球 10.7 亿美元）。在此之前，索尼电影还没有在第二个周末获得过 1 亿美元的票房。它差点就打破了 2015 年大二电影票房最高记录：《原力觉醒》，票房为 1.492 亿美元。
克里斯托弗·诺兰的《奥德赛》票房也突破了10亿美元。在上映的第四个周末，环球影业的国内票房收入增加了 3,150 万美元，全球总票房达到 11 亿美元。
诺兰的荷马史诗是自 2012 年《黑暗骑士崛起》以来导演第一部达到这一门槛的电影。现在，在不考虑通货膨胀的情况下，它成为诺兰有史以来票房最高的影片，超过了《黑暗骑士崛起》（10.8 亿美元）和 2009 年的《黑暗骑士》（10 亿美元）。诺兰的《奥本海默》（9.75 亿美元）以略低于里程碑的成绩结束。
当然，这一成功很大一部分归功于 IMAX。《奥德赛》在该公司的大屏幕上获得了 1.473 亿美元的国内票房，现已成为 IMAX 有史以来票房最高的国内影片。
《奥德赛》还剩下一个主要市场。该片将于周五在中国上映。
《蜘蛛侠：全新的一天》和《奥德赛》帮助好莱坞创下了自疫情以来的最佳票房年度。根据 Rentrak 的数据，门票销售量比去年增长了 18.5%。已经有五部票房达到 10 亿美元的电影——比 2019 年以来的任何一年都要多。另外两部是《迈克尔》和《超级马里奥银河电影》。
Rentrak 预测周一夏季影院的整体收入将达到 40 亿美元。长期以来，这种季节性标记一直是好莱坞业务蓬勃发展的标志。自疫情爆发以来，唯一一个票房收入超过 40 亿美元的夏季是 2023 年，当时《芭比娃娃》和《奥本海默》带动了票房收入。
根据 Rentrak 的数据，截至周日，夏季收入仅比 40 亿美元少 1,480 万美元。
两部喜剧试图为大片提供一些反制方案，但收效甚微。
威尔·格鲁克 (Will Gluck) 执导的浪漫喜剧《仅限一夜》(One Night Only) 规定婚前性行为为非法，每年只有一晚除外，首映票房为 570 万美元。环球影业发行的影片由莫妮卡·巴巴罗和卡勒姆·特纳主演，制作成本约为 2500 万美元。评论不好（烂番茄上有 46% 的新鲜度），但观众评分（CinemaScore 为“B+”）较好。
排在第四位的是福克斯探照灯公司的《超级士兵 3》，这是喜剧剧团 Broken Lizard 的长篇喜剧系列中的第三部。它首映票房为400万美元。
两部新的限量上映电影挤满了影院。A24 的《托尼》由多米尼克·塞萨 (Dominic Sessa) 饰演年轻的安东尼·波登 (Anthony Bourdain)，票房收入为 348,955 美元，成为年度最佳银幕平均首映票房之一：每家影院 58,159 美元。Mubi 的《瘴气营的青少年性与死亡》由《我看到了电视的光芒》的电影制片人简·舍恩布伦 (Jane Schoenbrun) 执导，首映后在五个银幕上的平均票房为 50,300 美元。
根据 Rentrak 的数据，随着周一公布的最终国内数据，该清单考虑了美国和加拿大影院周五至周日的预计门票销售情况：
1.《蜘蛛侠：崭新的一天》，1.45亿美元。

item.title: Blink-182 的 Travis Barker 差点丧命。一部新纪录片庆祝了他之前和之后的生活
item.description:
纽约（美联社）——《特拉维斯·巴克：比恐惧更响亮》上映三分钟后，屏幕上熊熊燃烧。从警车上调取的行车记录仪镜头显示了这场大火：那是 2008 年，巴克在南卡罗来纳州的一场空难中幸存下来。其他四个人没有。
然后，一刀切。这部纪录片讲述了 Blink-182 鼓手从 2017 年到 2026 年的故事，庆祝了巴克在这场改变生活的事故前后的生活，这是他职业生涯中的一个核心事件。这部电影一开始是他 2015 年回忆录《我能说：活得大、欺骗死亡和鼓、鼓、鼓》的镜像，但在制片人建议影片以巴克走向飞机的形象结尾后，影片就完全变成了另一回事。当时，巴克因创伤后应激障碍而无法飞行。
以“这件事仍然对我有影响力”作为结尾，他不太舒服。相反，他在最后登上了飞机，但纪录片的最终图像是家庭照片的幻灯片，包括他的妻子考特尼·卡戴珊和孩子们。
“我差点就死了，”他说。“分享我的生活可能会有帮助。”
特拉维斯·巴克 (Travis Barker) 于 2026 年 6 月 11 日星期四在纽约摆姿势拍照。（摄影：Matt Licari/Invision/美联社）
巴克的简历很长，一部两个半小时的纪录片只能涵盖这么多。这部电影抓住了大部分的要点，很快就将巴克塑造成一个叛逆的孩子，从他 4 岁得到他的第一套鼓到现在 50 岁，他拥有超自然的击鼓能力。
这中间还有许多项目：从他在担任垃圾收集者时加入的南加州朋克乐队 Feeble，到他在斯卡乐队 The Aquabats 中的表现，以及多白金唱片、流行朋克传奇人物 Blink-182——正是这支乐队让巴克一跃成为超级巨星。
还覆盖？他对滑板和汽车文化的热爱、他的服装品牌、业余项目 Box Car Racer 和 +44、转盘二人组 TRV$DJAM、嘻哈音乐（Bun B、Lil Wayne）等方面的各种实验和合作。
但这一切都是从打鼓开始的，有趣的是，《布偶》中的动物——他的第一个鼓手英雄——直到他发现了跨流派的伟大人物，如爵士乐传奇人物巴迪·里奇、丹尼斯·钱伯斯和埃尔文·琼斯以及莫特利·克鲁的汤米·李。
“打鼓对我来说真正重要的是在我妈妈去世后，所以这是一种治疗，”他回忆起自己的童年时说道。“这就像我的生活。对我来说就像氧气。”
这也是一种运动。巴克长期以来一直是一位专注的运动打击乐手，他将其比作拳击手的冥想状态。“这就像当你看到一名拳击手，他在第一轮就试图破发一样。有时我就是有这样的感觉，”他说。“有什么东西占据了我的身体。”
生活中的许多事件都威胁到了这种欣快感，但没有一个像飞机失事那样在身体上如此。“我在烧伤中心靠吗啡呆了六个月，做了 30 次手术，”他回忆道。“我身体百分之七十都被烧伤了。”一度，他不仅担心自己能否再次打鼓，甚至连走路都成了一个问号。
特拉维斯·巴克 (Travis Barker) 于 2026 年 6 月 11 日星期四在纽约摆姿势拍照。（摄影：Matt Licari/Invision/美联社）
甚至在事故发生之前，巴克的生活——尽管一直以音乐上的胜利为标志——就提供了关于韧性的教训。
“无论是我母亲的去世还是我的飞机失事，通过观察我的朋友和生活，我了解到，我看到创伤性经历要么摧毁一个人，要么定义他们，”他说。“我所经历的每一次失败，或者我所经历的每一次失败，都让我变得更加坚强。当时，我无法意识到这一点，对吧？我不想真正把自己的注意力集中在它上面。但是......这就是为什么我如此努力，我如此坚定地演奏音乐，如此坚定地要成功。B计划只是让A计划发挥作用。你知道吗？没有B计划。”
同样的坚韧也体现在他的清醒和对再次飞行的奉献上——这是他家人鼓励的一次旅程。“我现在一直在飞行，感觉很不稳定，我什至无法告诉你我脑子里在想什么。我只要看一眼，我妻子就没事，”他说。“我儿子很喜欢飞机，玩飞机，很天真，很美。”
“他们是我最大的快乐，”他谈到他的孩子们时说，他们在电影近十年的拍摄过程中在银幕上长大。
作为一个失去了很多并思考失去更多会是什么样子的人，当谈到遗产这个话题时，巴克有一个简单的梦想。“我想我希望人们记住我的音乐和击鼓，以及成为一个伟大的父亲、丈夫、儿子和兄弟，”他说。
至于医生？“也许我的故事对某人有帮助，”他停顿了一下。“我不喜欢发生的一切。我不喜欢所发生的损失。但我喜欢我必须努力工作。我喜欢我不是含着金汤匙出生的。我喜欢我必须导航并找到自己的路。整个旅程非常棒。”

item.title: 随着油价上涨，美国股市接近历史最高纪录
item.description:
纽约（美联社）——美国股市周一接近历史高点，而由于霍尔木兹海峡何时重新开放以及全球原油流动何时恢复的不确定性，油价上涨。
标准普尔 500 指数在小幅上涨和下跌之间翻转后下跌 0.1%，脱离了上周五创下的纪录。截至下午 2 点 03 分，道琼斯工业平均指数下跌 133 点，即 0.3%。东部时间，纳斯达克综合指数下跌0.4%。
在美国大公司利润飙升推动股市上涨后，股市动能正在放缓。据 FactSet 称，报告预计将显示标准普尔 500 指数成分股公司春季每股收益较上年同期增长 50%。这将是五年前以来的最佳增长，当时经济正在摆脱新冠疫情造成的鸿沟。
伯克希尔哈撒韦公司是上季度利润高于分析师预期的最新公司之一，这家由传奇投资者沃伦·巴菲特创建的公司周末表示，在新任首席执行官格雷格·阿贝尔的领导下，该公司还将部分巨额现金投资于股票。
伯克希尔·哈撒韦公司一向以低价购买股票而闻名，人们对美国股票普遍看起来太贵的批评很高。但当他们报告强劲的利润时，这有助于他们看起来不那么昂贵。
伯克希尔哈撒韦公司的股价上涨了 1.4%，其庞大的规模使其成为推动标准普尔 500 指数上涨的最强劲力量之一。
美国股市正在接近历史最高纪录。
MarineMax 股价上涨 45.8%，此前这家零售商、码头运营商和超级游艇服务提供商表示，同意以约 15 亿美元现金将自己出售给 Blackstone 旗下的一家投资组合公司。
Teledyne Technologies 表示将以每股 18.90 美元现金收购这家 X 射线成像组件制造商后，Varex Imaging 股价跃升 48.7%。
科技股是市场上权重最大的股票。英伟达下跌 2.5%，苹果下跌 2%。
英特尔表示可能出售价值 150 亿美元的股票，股价下跌 3.4%。此举将稀释现有投资者的所有权股份，英特尔表示，它可能会利用这笔现金进行投资，以利用人工智能技术方面正在进行的巨额支出。
石油市场上，每桶布伦特原油价格上涨 4.7%，至 87.50 美元。上个月，随着人们对美国和伊朗能够达成协议，允许油轮再次自由离开中东，向全球运送原油的希望不断升温，油价在 72 美元至 102 美元之间波动。
但希望再次转向谨慎，布伦特原油价格回到了本月早些时候、7月中旬、6月中旬和3月战争第一周的水平。
油价上涨推高通胀，本周华尔街的主要事件可能是周三有关上个月通胀情况的最新消息。经济学家预计通胀率将从 6 月份的 3.5% 放缓至 3.4%。
经济放缓意味着美联储加息的压力较小。较高的利率将有助于抑制通货膨胀，但也会使美国家庭和企业的借贷成本更高，从而减缓经济发展。他们还将降低股票和其他投资的价格。
周五的一份报告显示，美国各地的招聘意外疲软，降低了华尔街对即将加息的预期。但根据芝商所的数据，交易员仍认为美联储在 9 月份的下一次会议上加息的可能性仍为 50%。
周五晚间，10 年期国债收益率从 4.65% 升至 4.70%。这比与伊朗战争前的 3.97% 有所上升，而且抵押贷款和其他类型贷款的利率已经更高。
在国外股市，亚洲大部分地区指数上涨后，欧洲股市涨跌互现。日本日经 225 指数上涨 2.1%，成为全球最大的涨幅之一。
